item.title: “Cash Money & No Limit Tour” Sunrise Show Canceled, Refunds Detailed
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: The Cash Money & No Limit Tour's November 6 Sunrise show was canceled. The arena outlined refund steps for ticket holders.
item.content:encoded:
Birdman and Master P’s “Cash Money & No Limit Tour” will not reach Sunrise, Florida, on November 6. Amerant Bank Arena listed the show as canceled and posted refund instructions for fans who bought tickets.

The arena’s notice cited “unforeseen circumstances” without giving a more specific reason. The Friday concert was set for 8 p.m., with Boosie billed as a special guest. No replacement date appears in the notice.

The arena said refunds were available through the original seller and could take up to 30 days. SeatGeek customers do not need to file a request; their refunds will be automatic.

Fans who used resale sites, including StubHub, Vivid Seats or Ticketmaster, should contact those companies’ customer service teams. Anyone who bought tickets at the arena’s box office window should call 954-835-SHOW to provide refund information.

There is still conflicting information online. Promoter BMN Entertainment’s individual Sunrise page continues to display November 6, while its main tour itinerary leaves Sunrise out. The venue’s own page explicitly marks the show canceled.

Before the run, Master P discussed the joint tour and independent business with DJ Greg Street in an August interview for V-103 Atlanta.

The pairing brought artists from both New Orleans labels onto one arena bill. The announced lineup included Juvenile, Mannie Fresh and B.G. alongside No Limit names such as Silkk The Shocker and Mia X. BMN Entertainment promoted the run.

In explaining the collaboration, Birdman and Slim Williams previously described the tour as a celebration of their New Orleans roots and a chance to bring longtime fans together.

The tour began September 11 at Houston’s Toyota Center, then headed to New Orleans the next night. At that hometown stop, B.G. proposed to Brooke Jones onstage at Smoothie King Center. She accepted.

For fans looking at other dates, the promoter’s current schedule still lists Tampa’s Benchmark International Arena on November 7 and Raleigh’s Lenovo Center on November 8, both at 8 p.m.

The remaining listed stops are Chicago’s Wintrust Arena on November 13, Cincinnati’s Heritage Bank Center on November 14 and Cleveland’s Rocket Arena on November 15. Chicago and Cincinnati are set for 8 p.m.; Cleveland is listed for 7 p.m.

item.title: Trump Calls Nicki Minaj Press Secretary Idea Good, Says He Will Think About It
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Donald Trump said he would think about Nicki Minaj as White House press secretary after staffers floated the rapper for the job.
item.content:encoded:
Donald Trump called the idea of Nicki Minaj becoming White House press secretary a good one, giving his own answer after members of his team floated the rapper for the job.

The president addressed the suggestion in an interview with political commentator Benny Johnson. He said he would think about it but did not announce an appointment, according to Parade.

“That’s a good idea. I think I’ll have to think about that,” Trump said, according to TMZ. He also suggested Johnson for the role.

The answer put Trump himself into a conversation that had already moved from an Air Force One video to political reactions. His comments stopped short of offering Minaj the job or confirming that she would take over White House briefings.

The earlier talk followed her exchange with White House communications director Steven Cheung. In a video he posted October 25, Cheung questioned Minaj aboard Air Force One about the economy, polling and Trump’s campaign workload.

Cheung followed up by floating Minaj for the White House role in the message he posted with the video. Minaj was traveling with Trump to a Michigan rally and praised the amount of work he put into campaigning.

She shared Cheung’s post and tied her support to Trump’s business background. Minaj said his recovery from financial problems gave her confidence in his ability to manage the country’s finances. She also praised his stamina and his efforts to get other Republicans elected.

The staffers’ earlier suggestion had already drawn a response from California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s press office: “We can only pray.” That reply concerned the staff-generated job talk before Trump’s interview response.

Minaj’s involvement with the administration has also included small-business promotion. As AllHipHop previously reported, she appeared with Small Business Administration chief Kelly Loeffler during a September interview with Laura Ingraham. Minaj joined Grant Cardone and Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia as judges for the Million Dollar Pitch Competition, which offered a $1 million prize.

At the October 25 rally in Port Huron, Michigan, she urged voters to back Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 midterms. She also pledged to support Trump if he ran again.

item.title: Maino Says 50 Cent Fell Off, But Joe Budden Isn’t Buying It
item.dc:creator: yourfavenightmare
item.description: Maino questioned 50 Cent’s current rap skills, but Joe Budden is not going for it.
item.content:encoded:
Maino apparently thinks 50 Cent’s pen could use a tuneup, and he picked the right room to announce it.

During a recent episode of Let’s Rap About It, the conversation turned to rappers whose abilities have deteriorated over time. Joe Budden, appearing as a guest, suggested he could still approach his prime form if he returned to recording. That opened the door for a discussion about who actually lost a step.

Maino put 50 Cent’s name on the table. Joe wasn’t accepting that nomination.

Now, you can probably imagine why this particular selection comes with a little extra seasoning. Maino and the podcast crew already have friction with Curtis. Maino maintained that the tension wasn’t driving his assessment, even saying, “I love 50 Cent.” When Budden brought up 50’s television theme songs, Maino joked about cutting his microphone off.

That is one way to handle a rebuttal. The sound engineer suddenly becomes the most powerful person in the debate.

But Joe’s position gives this conversation somewhere interesting to go. Does a rapper lose his ability, or do listeners stop getting the kind of records that made them fans? Those are separate questions, and I would like somebody to bring a playlist before we start confiscating pens.

With 50, the expectations are enormous. People aren’t measuring him against an anonymous Tuesday afternoon freestyle. They are measuring him against the version of 50 that made an entire generation memorize his hooks.

Still, Maino is entitled to hear a decline. Joe is equally entitled to disagree. Hip-Hop would be considerably less entertaining if everybody arrived at the podcast with matching opinions and a fruit basket.

The existing dispute makes the exchange harder to hear as a purely musical critique, even with Maino denying that connection. Fair or unfair, listeners are going to consider the history. 

And let’s remember, these guys already put their grievances over beats. 50 Cent’s record and video with Max B took aim at the podcast circle, and Maino answered with “Bleed Like Us.” This argument had already traveled from the phone to the recording booth.

Personally, I would welcome the music. Let the next verse do the arguing.

Excerpt: Maino questioned 50 Cent’s current rap skills, but Joe Budden pushed back during a podcast exchange complicated by an existing feud.

item.title: Snoop Dogg Picks Violinist For $30,000 Ice Cream Job
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Snoop Dogg picked Australian violinist Annabelle Traves for a three-month Dr. Bombay ice cream tasting job worth $30,000.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg found a new hire for Dr. Bombay in the concert world, choosing Australian violinist Annabelle Traves for a three-month ice cream tasting job worth $30,000.

The Dubai-based musician landed the remote role after a search that drew more than 350,000 applicants. Hiring partner Deel announced her selection on October 28. The contract pays $10,000 a month.

Her concert career has included Carnegie Hall in New York. Traves used her violin to make her case. According to SmartCompany, her application included a version of “Young, Wild & Free,” the Snoop, Wiz Khalifa and Bruno Mars hit.

The outlet reported that recruiters cut the field to 50 people and interviewed each finalist. Snoop delivered the news to Traves himself in a video message made for her.

She told SmartCompany she considered acting as though she knew the finer points of making ice cream. Instead, she built her entry around music. Her advice from the experience was to use her strengths and put herself forward, even with long odds.

“I’ve spent my life training my ear, so I’m hoping my palate holds up to the same standard!” Traves said in a statement carried by Restaurant & Café.

Her assignment includes finding ideas for international flavors and helping develop an ice cream tied to Deel as Dr. Bombay explores new markets.

The distance had raised a practical question for Traves. She told SmartCompany she wondered whether an Australian living in Dubai without a U.S. visa could take the job. Deel had her signed up within 48 hours.

Dr. Bombay had already taken another step beyond supermarket shelves this year. As AllHipHop reported, the brand opened a Venice Beach storefront on April 19 beside Marathon Burger. Lil Baby joined the business as an investor and co-founder. That shop was announced as a venture running through October.

The beach location gave customers a place devoted to the brand, whose flavors included Baked Blueberry Muffin and peanut butter varieties. The boardwalk opening was billed as its first physical storefront.

Traves already had Australian desserts in mind. She told SmartCompany that lamington or pavlova could be ideas to try.

item.title: Are The Eagles Quietly Protesting Over Jalen Hurts’ Treatment?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: The Eagles’ struggles have sparked an uncomfortable & unconfirmed protest theory, but Jalen Hurts’ situation raises real questions about player care.
item.content:encoded:
Not too long ago, the Philadelphia Eagles were Super Bowl champions, and Jalen Hurts was the king of the kingdom. Now, we’re watching a season that has people asking what in the world happened.

After that championship, members of the team visited Donald Trump at the White House. Hurts did not attend. I’m not blaming the Orange Man for what’s happening on a football field, but this has certainly been a strange ride since that championship parade. That curse they talk about seems to be real though.

The rumor I’m hearing now is more straightforward: Could some Eagles players be expressing frustration with the organization through how they’re approaching this season?

Specifically, could there be resentment over how the team handled Hurts’ medical situation?

Let’s get the timeline right. According to the Eagles, Hurts reported a calf injury before the trip to London, but an ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot after the team arrived. The organization says its medical staff and doctors in London cleared him to play. He subsequently played against Jacksonville and flew home. A follow-up ultrasound later showed movement in the clot. 

Further evaluations revealed deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs. The Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn, said he was clinically stable and expected to make a full recovery. His treatment involves blood thinners, which prevent him from participating in contact activities while taking them. He is expected to miss the remainder of the season.

That is bigger than football.

The NFL and NFL Players Association are reviewing how the situation was handled. That review does not establish wrongdoing, but it means the questions surrounding his care have reached beyond frustrated fans.

Now, put yourself in a player’s position. You might look at what happened to your quarterback and wonder whether something similar could happen to you. You might have questions about the decisions being made around your health.

I certainly would.

And we’re talking about Jalen Hurts. He’s the leader! From where I’m sitting, he represents a huge part of this team’s identity. Losing him under these circumstances could shake a locker room, even without anybody organizing a rebellion.

Watching the defense struggle, I found myself wondering where the intensity went. There have been stretches when that unit looked capable of keeping Philadelphia in games almost by itself. Then you watch another performance and ask, “Where did those guys go?”

But looking flat and deliberately refusing to compete are two very different accusations. I haven’t seen verified evidence that players have agreed to stop playing hard, boycott games or tank the season.

What I’m hearing is a theory about frustration with head coach Nick Sirianni or the organization. Whether that reflects anything actually happening inside the building remains unconfirmed.

Sirianni has defended the team’s handling of Hurts’ situation, saying he relies on medical experts and trusts the people making those decisions. He has also maintained that player health comes first. 

There’s another piece of talk floating around, too: that some players may be less willing to compete through injuries.

Again, I cannot confirm that this is happening as an organized show of solidarity. An injury report alone cannot tell us why someone sits out or whether he could safely play.

And honestly, if a player is hurt and needs to sit, that decision doesn’t require a secret protest to explain it. These guys have careers, families and lives after football to consider.

Still, trust is a fair subject to discuss. If players lose confidence in the people responsible for their care, how does that affect the locker room? How does it affect their willingness to push through discomfort? Those are questions worth asking without pretending we already know the answers.

It is also entirely possible that the Eagles are simply having a terrible season. Injuries, execution, coaching and the loss of their starting quarterback could explain plenty.

As an Eagles fan, I’m frustrated. I’m watching, listening and trying to understand how things got here. I’m keeping the protest theory on the table as an unconfirmed possibility, but I need more than bad football before calling this a rebellion.

The Eagles’ recent championship history explains why this downturn feels so jarring. Philadelphia defeated Kansas City 40-22 in Super Bowl LIX on February 9, 2025, denying the Chiefs a third consecutive title. Hurts earned the game’s Most Valuable Player award after throwing for 221 yards and two touchdowns while adding 72 rushing yards and another score. Philadelphia’s defense was central to that victory, pressuring Patrick Mahomes and helping establish a commanding lead. That performance set a standard for this roster and its coaching staff. Fans remember a complete team, which makes today’s uncertainty especially difficult for them to process.

What do you think? Are the Eagles dealing with a crisis of trust, or are we watching a struggling team search for answers? Comment your thoughts below.

item.title: Skilla Baby Gets Ford Field Pregame Spotlight
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Skilla Baby will perform before kickoff at Ford Field on November 1, sharing the music lineup with halftime act The Four Tops.
item.content:encoded:
Skilla Baby has a hometown stadium date on his calendar. The Detroit rapper will perform before kickoff at Ford Field on Sunday, November 1.

The Lions announced the booking Thursday, according to the Detroit Free Press. The Four Tops have a separate halftime set, putting Detroit rap and Motown on the same afternoon’s music lineup.

Jack White and The Temptations performed at halftime at Ford Field during the 2025 season.

The appearance comes during the rollout for The Price Of Fame, his debut studio album. The project arrived in August with guests including Nas, Bryson Tiller, Chris Brown and Erica Campbell. That mix brought veteran rap, R&B and gospel voices into his latest release.

Skilla Baby also teamed with Live Nation Urban for “The Price Of Fame Tour,” a run of headlining dates announced in August. The route stretches beyond his home region, with stops listed in Texas, California and the Midwest.

Before the album came out, he spoke about what making it meant to him. In footage covered by AllHipHop in August, Skilla Baby said the work helped him through mental health struggles. He wanted fans to hear about his better days as well as the low points he had shared.

Nas appeared in a promotional conversation for the project and urged him to value family, self-respect and knowledge alongside success. He also warned against measuring his own progress against what other people posted on Instagram. The exchange offered a look at the advice behind the collaboration.

His life away from the stage has included showing up for young people, too. AllHipHop previously reported that he visited Compton College about a week after being shot in 2025. He was still recovering when he attended the Make Your Own Way Foundation event.

Manager Roccett told AllHipHop that Skilla Baby gave students clothes and talked about staying in school and avoiding street life. His team had wanted him to keep resting, Roccett said, but the rapper insisted on honoring the commitment.

For Detroit fans, the stadium booking comes ahead of another local date. His tour schedule lists The Fillmore Detroit on November 22, giving his hometown audience a full headlining show later in the month.

item.title: Latto Weighs Charging For Features
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Latto said she has done features for free when she likes the music, but having a baby has her weighing a change in business.
item.content:encoded:
Latto said she has done guest verses for free when she likes the song and artist, but motherhood has her thinking about a fee.

During her October 29 appearance on “Hot Ones,” she told Sean Evans that other artists charge her.

“But I’ve been thinking about that now that I got a baby to feed,” she said.

She described those collaborations as favors, with the music coming first. She raised the question of charging without naming a price.

The interview also covered her critics. Latto said negative comments push her to prove people wrong. That included defending the food she shares through her “Soul Food Sunday” posts after people criticized her gumbo.

Her own recent records show how much of her work involves other artists. Big Mama, her fourth studio album, arrived on May 29 with 18 tracks. GloRilla joined her on “GOMF,” while Doja Cat appeared on “Okayyy” and 21 Savage on “Hostage.” The album also paired her with Sexyy Red for “Need Luv 2” and Mariah the Scientist for “Make Me.”

That guest list reached beyond rap. Odeal and Wizkid appeared together on “Anxious,” Teyana Taylor joined “4L” and Jelly Roll featured on “Mama.” According to Sony Music’s album announcement, Latto learned she was pregnant while making the project, bringing that change in her life into the recording process.

The release followed Sugar Honey Iced Tea in 2024. That album reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Rap Albums chart, making her the first solo female rapper from Atlanta to lead it. Her 2022 album 777 had reached No. 6 on that chart.

The pushback over her cooking also fits a longer history of answering personal criticism in public. In May 2024, she responded to body-shaming after clips from her TwoGether Land Festival set in Dallas drew comments about her BBL. She followed with photos on Instagram and a message on X saying her partner was happy with her looks. The criticism followed her performance of “Sunday Service.”

Her work with Doja Cat also extends to the stage. T-Mobile Arena lists Latto on Doja Cat’s “Tour Ma Vie World Tour” stop in Las Vegas on October 31, with the show set for 7:30 P.M.

item.title: Michael Jackson, Superheroes & The Weird Costumes Make 2026 Halloween Cool
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” look surges as Halloween 2026 mixes classic costumes, superhero favorites and viral hits.
item.content:encoded:
It’s Big Michael Michael!

Michael Jackson’s red jacket is having another moment. Spider-Man still rules the neighborhood. And a creepy unicorn has crashed the Halloween conversation.

In a year where reality feels like a horror movie, we get costumes that reflect more hopeful sentiments. This year’s costume picture blends familiar favorites with unexpected newcomers. We delved into some experts on trends. The National Retail Federation measures what consumers plan to wear, while Google’s Frightgeist tracks rising costume searches. We used both to come up with this master list. They offer a broader view of Halloween 2026, from reliable crowd favorites to characters inspiring fresh curiosity. We skipped the celebrity showings for now.

This is an editorial mix that begins with the King of Pop, who has posthumously had a banner year.

Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” Look

The red jacket remains unmistakable. Jackson ranks on Google’s trending list, and searches for his costumes have reached a 10-year high. We’ve already seen a lot of MJ thanks to LooseCannon and Big Michael Michael. Some Halloween traditions moonwalk through generations. 

Spider-Man

The neighborhood superhero remains the leading children’s choice. NRF estimates 4.6 million kids plan to dress as Spider-Man, with another 1.5 million adults joining the web-slinging action.

Witches

Pointed hats still mean business. Approximately 4.8 million adults plan to dress as witches, putting the classic character ahead of the competition in NRF’s survey.

Vampires

Fangs never seem to lose their audience. An estimated 4.2 million adults plan to embrace the vampire look, making it another major Halloween staple.

Batman

Gotham’s protector ranks third among adult choices. Approximately 2 million adults plan to become Batman, proving the cape and cowl still command attention.

Buddy The Unicorn

Here comes the curveball. The character from the horror film Buddy leads Google’s trending costume searches, giving Halloween a colorful option with an unsettling edge.

KPop Demon Hunters

Music, animation and supernatural action remain a compelling combination. Characters from KPop Demon Hunters land among NRF’s top 10 children’s costumes, maintaining their appeal beyond last year’s search buzz. 

NeeDoh

Yes, the squishy toy. NeeDoh ranks second on Google’s trending list, making stress relief an unexpectedly prominent source of Halloween inspiration. How though?

Nikki From Obsession

Nikki takes third place among Google’s trending costumes. The character from Obsession gives horror fans another option beyond the familiar masks that return every October. That movie was incredible.

Disco Scooby-Doo

Scooby brings nostalgia and dance-floor energy. This playful variation ranks high on Google’s list and offers a recognizable foundation for a costume with personality. Personally, this is a hard pass.

Dolly Parton

Big hair and country glamour earn a place in the conversation. Parton ranks 12th on Google’s overall trending list, adding another music legend to Halloween’s lineup.

Ghosts

Roughly 1.4 million adults and 1.6 million children plan to dress as ghosts. Sometimes the easiest costume remains one of the biggest. 

The Notable Absences

Labubu dominated Google’s 2025 Halloween highlights but is absent from its 2026 overall top 25. Barbie, Ken and Wednesday Addams are also missing from that breakout list. 

For now, Michael Jackson’s comeback, Dolly’s passing and Halloween’s dependable classics give everybody something refreshed or new.

item.title: French Montana & D-Block Europe Tour Cancellations Reach Seven Shows
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: French Montana and D-Block Europe have seven canceled European shows, with Prague, Warsaw and Berlin joining the list.
item.content:encoded:
French Montana and D-Block Europe fans in Prague, Warsaw and Berlin will miss their planned joint concerts, adding three more cities to the run of canceled European dates.

Seven stops on the “Worldwide Wave Tour” are canceled, according to TicketNews. The affected bookings stretch from October 30 through November 8, across seven countries. The report reviewed venue and ticketing records to establish how much of the continental run was off.

Prague’s November 1 show was booked at SaSaZu Club. Ticketing platform Eventlook marks the concert canceled on its listing of events at the club. The scheduled start was 8 P.M. and the listing had advertised tickets from 840 Czech koruna. No replacement date appears alongside the canceled entry.

Warsaw was next on the calendar, with French and the British duo booked for November 2 at Progresja. Polish ticket seller eBilet labels that date canceled and identifies Live Nation as the organizer. Its page still carries promotional background about the artists beneath the cancellation status, but the ticket section places the concert among unavailable dates.

Berlin’s Uber Eats Music Hall also confirms that the November 5 concert is canceled. That venue gives buyers a direct instruction about their tickets.

“Tickets can be returned immediately at the location where they were purchased,” the hall says.

Those three cities extend the cancellations beyond the stops AllHipHop previously covered. Amsterdam and Vienna were booked for October 30 and November 6, respectively. Copenhagen’s Store VEGA date was November 4. Amsterdam ticket holders were told to expect an email from Ticketmaster with more information. Paris, scheduled for November 8 at Elysée Montmartre, is also marked canceled by Live Nation’s French site.

There is no stated common cause in TicketNews’ review of the seven dates. Amsterdam’s explanation of “unforeseen circumstances” does not establish why the other concerts were canceled.

The shared bill followed Worldwide Wave, the album French made with D-Block Europe. Apple Music lists its release as September 11, with 19 songs running 55 minutes. The duo consists of Young Adz and Dirtbike LB. The project includes “RICO” and “Rich Low Life,” with Max B featured on the latter, according to Apple’s album notes.

item.title: O’Shea Jackson Jr. Jokes He’ll Call Mom Over Ice Cube’s “Last Friday”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: O'Shea Jackson Jr. joked about calling his mom after his agent had no news about a role in Ice Cube's "Last Friday."
item.content:encoded:
O’Shea Jackson Jr. joked that he might bring his mother into the casting process for Ice Cube’s “Last Friday” after his agent had given him no word about the project.

The actor responded on X on October 27 to news that Lawrence Lamont would direct the next film in his father’s comedy series. According to TheWrap’s account of the post, he wrote, “….I haven’t received any emails or calls from my agent about this project….”

He ended the joke with a promise: “I will call mom.” Jackson is the oldest son of Cube and Kimberly Woodruff.

He already played his father in the 2015 N.W.A biopic “Straight Outta Compton.” His other screen credits include “Just Mercy,” “Cocaine Bear” and “Godzilla: King of the Monsters.” He also worked opposite Gerard Butler in the “Den of Thieves” movies.

“Last Friday” would be the fourth feature in a series that started in 1995. Cube created the original “Friday” with DJ Pooh, with F. Gary Gray directing.

Chris Tucker played Smokey alongside Cube, while John Witherspoon played the father of Cube’s character. The franchise later included comedians such as Mike Epps, Bernie Mac and Faizon Love. The most recent film, “Friday After Next,” came out in 2002, leaving a 24-year gap before this latest round of sequel news.

As AllHipHop previously reported, Lamont directed Keke Palmer and SZA in “One Of Them Days.” That comedy followed two friends trying to keep their home after their rent money went missing.

His work also includes videos for Big Sean and J. Cole, plus work on Issa Rae’s “Rap Sh!t.” The director announcement followed Cube’s July 17 appearance with Epps in Long Beach, where he told fans they had submitted the “Last Friday” script.

The project also received state support ahead of Jackson’s joke. On October 7, the California Film Commission named New Line Cinema’s “Last Friday” among 35 movies selected for production tax credits. The state identified Cube as the film’s star, writer and producer.

In that announcement, Cube said the Southern California production planned to employ more than 180 local cast and crew members. He tied the decision to shoot there to the original movie’s roots in South Los Angeles.
